subject.title: fix(reef): add timeout and bounded JSON reads to relay transport

question: Should Reef relay REST requests unconditionally fail after 15 seconds without response headers?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but the deadline is a new runtime default that can reject previously successful slow relays; repository evidence does not establish the Reef protocol's maximum legitimate header latency.

options.title: Approve the 15-second deadline
options.body: Accept the compatibility change because normal relay calls should return headers well inside 15 seconds and bounded recovery is preferable to an indefinite channel stall.

options.title: Align the deadline with owner policy
options.body: Change the constant to the Reef owner's established request budget, retaining the shared helper and the same regression coverage.

options.title: Pause the timeout change
options.body: Keep the PR open or close it if Reef relays may legitimately exceed a fixed deadline and no supported latency contract can be established.

recommendation.title: Approve the 15-second deadline
recommendation.body: Accept the compatibility change because normal relay calls should return headers well inside 15 seconds and bounded recovery is preferable to an indefinite channel stall.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently changed the same Reef request method on current main and have direct context on its transport and error-handling behavior.
